data.name: Pairs
data.detailed_description:
Check This Out!



Acerca do jogo

Pairs is a free visual novel. It was originally created for a game jam called NaNoRenO between March 1st and April 2nd. In October 2017, it was remastered with additional sprites, new dialogue and a marked lack of typos for release on Steam. Hopefully. We hope that you enjoy this version of the game!

Story:

Invaders from the stars come to conquer planet Earth, attempting to add the blue marble into it's vast network of conquered planets on their quest to rule over the known, weak universe. In an attempt to protect itself, humans around the world begin to manifest superhuman powers beyond the imagination, powers strong enough to combat their alien foes. Three generations later, the war wages on with the Naian forces showing no sign of let up....

But that is not the focus of our story.

Our story begins with four protagonists in pairs-- two couples who are dealing with largely different issues unique to their world.
  • Lek Noiya, heir to the Naian throne and a product of her violent culture, craves a human heart-- or a human's loyalty with her foot on his back.
  • James Zhang, a somewhat non-descript young man who seems a little too nonchalant about dating the daughter of Earth's sworn enemy, perhaps because he has an ulterior motive that's worth risking everything for.
  • Carmelita Brown, a superhuman trainee preparing for her life as a Certified Hero, dealing with the fact she's not sure how she feels about her decision for her best friend to become her boyfriend-- or the fact that despite it being her life passion, she's not as good as hero work as she'd like to be.
  • Ricardo Fernandez, Carmelita's fellow trainee and childhood best friend, a young man who excels at hero work but struggles with his unsure motivations for becoming a hero-- and the idea that staying by Carmelita's side is worth it when lately, she's been so cold towards him...

How will these relationships pan out?

Only time will tell in Pairs.


Features:
  • 2 distinct couple storylines with four protagonists: Noiya and James, Carmelita and Ricardo
  • 8 different endings, two for each protagonist
  • Roughly 70,000 words
  • Original Soundtrack with 7 unique tracks

reviews.review:
Pairs is a narrative-driven visual novel that blends romance, science fiction, and superhero themes into an unconventional exploration of human relationships. Developed and published by Jellyfish Parade, the game takes place in a world where humanity has spent generations resisting an invasion by an aggressive extraterrestrial civilization. Instead of concentrating on military conflicts or spectacular superhero battles, the experience examines the personal struggles of four individuals whose relationships are complicated by cultural differences, emotional insecurities, and conflicting ambitions. This character-focused approach gives the game a distinctive identity within the visual novel genre.

The story unfolds against the backdrop of an ongoing war between humanity and the Naian civilization, an expansionist alien empire determined to conquer Earth. Humanity's unexpected development of superhuman abilities has prevented complete domination, creating a prolonged conflict that has fundamentally transformed society. Despite this dramatic setting, the narrative emphasizes romance and personal development rather than conventional science-fiction action. The contrast between extraordinary circumstances and ordinary emotional problems establishes an intriguing foundation for the storytelling.

One of the central relationships involves Lek Noiya, an heir to the Naian throne, and James Zhang, a human whose romantic involvement with an extraterrestrial royal introduces considerable complications. Noiya comes from a civilization shaped by conquest and aggression, making her relationship with someone belonging to an opposing species particularly unusual. James appears surprisingly comfortable with their circumstances, although his motivations may be more complicated than they initially seem. Their storyline raises interesting questions about cultural incompatibility, trust, personal intentions, and whether genuine affection can overcome deeply rooted hostility.

The second relationship follows Carmelita Brown and Ricardo Fernandez, childhood friends pursuing careers as professional superheroes. Their romantic difficulties emerge from personal uncertainty rather than political conflict. Carmelita struggles with confidence in her abilities while questioning the stability of their relationship. Ricardo possesses considerable potential as a superhero but faces doubts about his motivations and emotional commitments. Their storyline offers a more relatable examination of insecurity, ambition, and the challenges of maintaining affection while pursuing individual aspirations.

The contrast between these relationships represents one of the game's most appealing qualities. While one couple must navigate extraordinary cultural and political barriers, the other faces emotional difficulties recognizable in everyday life. This dual perspective creates opportunities for meaningful character development and allows the narrative to explore different interpretations of love, loyalty, and responsibility. The protagonists' contrasting personalities also help distinguish their respective stories.

With approximately 70,000 words of narrative content, Pairs offers a substantial reading experience for players who appreciate dialogue-heavy storytelling. The game features eight endings, providing two possible conclusions for each protagonist. This structure encourages repeated playthroughs to discover alternative outcomes and examine how the characters' relationships develop. However, players expecting elaborate gameplay mechanics, extensive exploration, or interactive combat should understand that the experience primarily revolves around reading and following the narrative.

Visually, the game adopts a traditional visual novel presentation, relying on character illustrations and dialogue to communicate emotional developments. Improvements made beyond its original game-jam version include additional character sprites, expanded conversations, and proofreading adjustments. These refinements contribute to a more complete presentation, although the game's relatively modest production scope remains apparent. Its appeal consequently depends more on the quality of its storytelling than on technical sophistication or elaborate visual effects.

The soundtrack consists of seven original musical compositions intended to accompany the narrative's emotional atmosphere. Music can provide valuable support during romantic conversations, moments of uncertainty, and dramatic revelations. Nevertheless, the relatively small selection of tracks may become repetitive throughout an extended reading experience. The absence of extensive voice acting also places greater emphasis on written dialogue and character illustrations.

Another notable advantage is its free availability, making it accessible to anyone interested in exploring its unusual premise without financial commitment. Its lightweight system requirements and modest storage demands further increase accessibility. However, the game's heavy reliance on reading may limit its appeal among players seeking more mechanically engaging experiences. Additionally, the combination of superhero fiction, extraterrestrial politics, and relationship drama may not satisfy everyone equally, particularly those expecting the larger conflict to dominate the narrative.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, Pairs does not have a confirmed official Steam Deck Verified or Playable classification. Its lightweight requirements, Linux support, and visual novel gameplay suggest that it could potentially function on Valve's handheld system. However, controller compatibility, interface scaling, and text readability have not been conclusively established. Players should therefore consider its Steam Deck compatibility unverified rather than assume completely trouble-free operation.

Overall, Pairs offers an interesting interpretation of romantic storytelling within a science-fiction universe. Its strongest qualities include its unusual premise, contrasting character relationships, substantial narrative content, and multiple endings. Although its limited gameplay interaction and modest audiovisual presentation may discourage players seeking greater mechanical depth, its emphasis on emotional complexity provides a worthwhile experience for visual novel enthusiasts. The combination of personal struggles and extraordinary circumstances makes it an appealing choice for readers interested in unconventional romance narratives.

Pairs is an engaging concept-driven visual novel that prioritizes character relationships and emotional storytelling over action. Its accessible format, multiple endings, and distinctive setting make it worth considering for fans of narrative adventures.

Rating: 7/10
